front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** ("the Agency") operates as a Private Home Care Provider (PHCP) licensed by the Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH), Healthcare Facility Regulation Division, under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65. It covers the Agency's nursing, personal care, and companion/sitter services. Where the Agency participates in Medicaid home and community-based programs, it also covers the Elderly and Disabled Waiver (CCSP/SOURCE), ICWP, and NOW/COMP community living supports.

The manual has five aims:

- **Meet licensure requirements.** The rules require written policies and procedures on the scope of services and types of clients served, service agreements, record keeping and confidentiality, staffing, training, supervision, service plans, client rights and complaints, and quality improvement.
- **Support the governing body.** Rule 111-8-65-.04 makes the governing body responsible for determining all policies and procedures and for ensuring compliance with the rules. This manual is the written record of those decisions.
- **Protect clients.** It gives staff clear, consistent procedures for safe, respectful, and dependable in-home care. These include reporting changes in condition, handling medical emergencies, and reporting suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation.
- **Support program participation.** It helps the Agency meet the requirements of Medicaid waiver and Aging Services programs, including holding a current DCH private home care license and using Electronic Visit Verification (EVV).
- **Prepare for inspection.** It lets staff and surveyors see how the Agency meets each requirement, and it supports the written plan of correction if DCH cites deficiencies.

**This manual is a template and must be customized.** Every bracketed placeholder, such as **[AGENCY NAME]**, **[ADMINISTRATOR NAME]**, **[RN SUPERVISOR NAME]**, **[LICENSE NUMBER]**, and **[PHONE NUMBER]**, must be replaced with the Agency's own information. Policies must also be adjusted to match the services the Agency actually offers, the clients it serves, and the geographic area described in its license application. The rules prohibit offering services the Agency cannot reasonably deliver, so do not keep policy sections for services the Agency does not provide. This manual is a compliance tool and is not legal advice. The Agency should confirm its final policies with qualified counsel and, where needed, with DCH.

## How to Use This Manual

### Who should use it
- **Governing body and owners** use it to adopt, review, and approve policy.
- **The Administrator** uses it to run daily operations and to keep records, staffing, and supervision in compliance.
- **Nurse and other qualified supervisors** use it for service plans, supervisory visits, and staff evaluations.
- **Personal care assistants (PCAs), companions/sitters, and nursing staff** use it as their reference for duties, limits on tasks, documentation, reporting, and client rights.

### Before you use it: required steps
1. **Customize it.** Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** and other bracketed placeholder. Delete or revise sections that do not match the Agency's actual services, client types, or service area.
2. **Have the governing body adopt it.** Under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.04, the governing body must determine the Agency's policies and procedures. Record adoption in dated governing body minutes or a signed resolution. Record each later revision the same way.
3. **Train all staff on it.** Orientation before any client contact must cover the Agency's written policies on scope of services and client types, client rights and complaints, the employee's duties, reporting client progress and problems, handling medical emergencies and incidents, and the duty to report known exposure to TB or hepatitis (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(6)). Each employee must also receive at least 8 clock hours of annual training after the first year of employment. Keep signed acknowledgments and training documentation in each personnel record (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(4)(c)).
4. **Keep it current.** Review the manual at least annually, and whenever a rule, program requirement, service offering, or Agency practice changes. Update the effective date and version number, obtain governing body approval for each revision, and retrain staff on the changes. Keep superseded versions on file.
5. **Make it available.** Keep a current copy where staff and the Administrator can reach it, and have it ready for DCH inspectors. DCH has access to premises, records, staff, and consenting clients during regular business hours (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.08).

### How the manual is organized
Sections follow the structure of Rule 111-8-65 and the Agency's program obligations: governing body and licensure; administration and service agreements; client and personnel records; staffing, qualifications, and training; supervision and service plans; client rights and complaints; incident reporting and quality improvement; and Medicaid/EVV, adult protection reporting, and employment-related policies. Each policy should cite the rule or program requirement it implements, using the exact cite text listed in the Regulatory Framework section.

### Items flagged for verification
The research behind this manual identified a few points that must be confirmed before the related policies are finalized:
- **Administrator fingerprint records check.** The current Secretary of State text of Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(3)(a)1 includes a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination. Other versions of the rule may read differently. Confirm the current text with DCH.
- **Background check coverage.** Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. Chapter 111-8-12 applies to the owner before a new license issues. Which other positions are covered was not verified. Confirm with the Healthcare Facility Regulation Division.
- **Overtime policy.** The status of 29 CFR § 552.109(a) was not confirmed for 2026. Verify it before finalizing any overtime or wage policy.
- **Mandated reporters.** The full list of mandated reporters under O.C.G.A. § 30-5-4 was seen only in part. For that reason, this manual treats every caregiver as a reporter.
- **Regulator contact details.** Phone numbers and emails were not available for most regulators. Confirm current contact details on each regulator's website before publishing the manual.

## Regulatory Framework

The Agency operates under the authorities listed below. Cites are given exactly as they appear in the research record. Confirm the current text of each rule before relying on it.

### Licensure and governing rules: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65 (Private Home Care Providers)
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.01**: Legal Authority. The rules are adopted under O.C.G.A. § 31-7-300 et seq.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.03**: Definitions. These include companion or sitter tasks, home management (employees with unlimited access to client funds must be bonded through the provider), medically frail or compromised client, medically related activities, owner (10% or greater interest), personal care tasks, private home care provider and services, and transport and escort.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.04**: Governing Body. The governing body must determine all policies and procedures and ensure compliance with the rules.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.05**: Licenses. This covers the license requirement and provisional licenses, the owner's compliance with Chapter 111-8-12, separate licensing of each location, display of the license, non-transferability, and 15 days' advance notice to DCH of a location change.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.06**: Applications. This covers initial and renewal applications, fees, and truthfulness (a false statement can lead to license refusal).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.07**: Exemptions. This covers who is exempt, and notes that no Certificate of Need is required for a PHCP-only license.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.08**: Inspections and Plans of Correction. DCH may enter during regular business hours. Staff must cooperate without unreasonable delay. An acceptable written plan of correction is due within ten days of receiving the written report.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(1)**: Administration and Organization, Services Description.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(2)**: Administration and Organization, Service Agreements.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(3)**: Administration and Organization, Administrator.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(4)(a)**: Client Records.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(4)(b)**: Retention and Confidentiality of Client Records (minimum retention is five years from the last service).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(4)(c)**: Personnel Records.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(4)(d)**: Reports of Complaints and Incidents.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(5)(a)-(b)**: Staffing, General and Nursing Personnel.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(5)(c)**: Personal Care Assistant (PCA) Qualifications.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(5)(d)**: Companions or Sitters.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(6)**: Staff Training.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.09(7)**: Contracted Services.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.10(1)**: Categories of Services.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.10(2) (intro, (a))**: Supervision of Services; Nursing Supervision.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.10(2)(b)**: Supervision of Personal Care Tasks (supervisory home visit at least every 92 days).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.10(2)(c)**: Supervision of Companion or Sitter Tasks (supervisory home visit at least every 122 days).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.10(2)(d)**: On-call Representative for Medically Frail Clients.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.10(3)**: Documentation of Home Care Services Provided.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.10(4)**: Quality Improvement Program.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.11**: Service Plans.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.12**: Client Rights, Responsibilities, and Complaints.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.13**: Enforcement and Penalties. After notice and an opportunity for hearing, DCH may refuse, limit, restrict, suspend, revoke, or refuse to renew a license, issue a public reprimand, or impose a fine.

### Background checks
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. Chapter 111-8-12**: Rules and Regulations for Criminal Background Checks. The owner must comply before a new PHCP license is issued. Coverage of other positions was not verified. Confirm with the Healthcare Facility Regulation Division.

### Medicaid and Aging Services program requirements
- **DHS DAS HCBS 5300 Manual § 208**: In-Home Services. CCSP in-home service providers must hold a current, valid DCH private home care license.
- **Social Security Act § 1915(c); CMS Waiver 0112.R08.00**: Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver (CCSP/SOURCE). The waiver was approved 11/09/2022 to 11/08/2027. DCH handles reimbursement, enrollment, and utilization review. DAS runs day-to-day CCSP operations.
- **21st Century Cures Act (2016) § 12006 — EVV; Georgia DCH EVV program**: Electronic Visit Verification is required for Medicaid-financed personal care services. Georgia's system is Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+. Each visit records service type, recipient, provider, date, location, and start/end times. Billing codes: CCSP/SOURCE (IDs 590/930) T1019 with TF/UC; ICWP (660) and NOW/COMP (680/681) T2025.

### Adult protection and employment
- **O.C.G.A. § 30-5-4**: Reporting of need for protective services. A person with reasonable cause to believe a disabled adult or elder person has been abused, neglected, or exploited must report to the designated adult protection agency (DHS-DAS Adult Protective Services) and to an appropriate law enforcement agency or prosecutor. Staff of a hospital, social agency, financial institution, or similar facility must notify the person in charge, who reports or causes the report. Good-faith reporters are immune (§ 30-5-4(c)). Agency policy treats every caregiver as a reporter.
- **29 CFR § 552.109(a)**: Third-party employers of home care workers. Per the provided research, third-party employers (agencies) may not claim the companionship exemption from overtime. Its 2026 status was not confirmed. Verify before finalizing the overtime policy.

### Regulators and contacts
Phone numbers and emails were not available for most entries. Confirm current contact information on each website and enter it here when customizing the manual.

Licensure fees are set through the Board of Community Health. | https://dch.georgia.gov/divisionsoffices/hfrd/facilities-provider-information/private-home-care-program | [Confirm on website — not provided] |
| **Georgia DCH, Medical Assistance Plans (Georgia Medicaid)** | Provider reimbursement, enrollment, and utilization review for CCSP/SOURCE; GAMMIS claims; EVV program (Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+) | https://medicaid.georgia.gov/programs/all-programs/waiver-programs | (833) 483-5587 (Georgia EVV Customer Support; the old EVV number was retired Jan 16, 2026) |

| **Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs)** | DAS administers its programs through the AAAs, the access route for in-home services and waiver intake. | https://aging.georgia.gov/programs-and-services | [Confirm for your service area] |
| **Georgia Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities (DBHDD)** | Manages the NOW/COMP planning list and waiver slots (community living supports for people with I/DD) | https://www.open.georgia.gov/openga/report/downloadFile?rid=33476 | [Confirm on website — not provided] |

DHS-DAS Adult Protective Services and the appropriate local law enforcement agency or prosecutor are the reporting points under O.C.G.A. § 30-5-4. Enter their current contact information in **[APS HOTLINE / LAW ENFORCEMENT CONTACT]** when customizing this manual.

### Maintaining this framework
This manual must be customized for **[AGENCY NAME]**, adopted by its governing body under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. R. 111-8-65-.04, kept current as rules and program requirements change, and taught to all staff in orientation and annual training. Do not treat any rule summary above as a substitute for the full text. Confirm the current text on the Georgia Secretary of State rules site (https://rules.sos.ga.gov/gac/111-8-65) and with DCH.

citations.title: Legal Authority
citations.requirement: Rules are adopted under O.C.G.A. § 31-7-300 et seq.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines: applicant/licensee by entity type (.03(b)); companion or sitter tasks (.03(c)); home management, where any employee with unlimited access to client funds must be bonded through the provider (.03(g)); medically frail or compromised client (.03(j)); medically related activities, including reminding clients to take medication and assisting with self-administration, but excluding professional services (.03(k)); owner as any person with 10% or greater interest (.03(l)); personal care tasks (.03(n)); private home care provider and services (.03(o)-(p)); transport and escort, which requires a client waiver of claims or reasonable efforts to confirm motor vehicle insurance when the employee drives a vehicle not owned by the client (.03(s)).

citations.title: Governing Body
citations.requirement: Each provider must have a governing body empowered and responsible to determine all policies and procedures and to ensure compliance with the rules.

citations.title: Licenses
citations.requirement: No operation without a license or provisional license (.05(1)). Owner must comply with Chapter 111-8-12 before a new license issues (.05(1)(b)). A provisional license may be issued to a new provider for a limited time or to an existing provider with an acceptable plan of improvement (.05(1)(c)). Administrator and employees must be qualified (.05(2)). Each location is separately licensed (.05(2)(a)). The license must be displayed (.05(2)(b)). It is not assignable or transferable. It must be returned on change of name, location, ownership or governing body. DCH must get 15 days' advance notice of a location change (.05(2)(c)).

citations.title: Applications
citations.requirement: Initial application on DCH forms, with application fee, Board-set license fee, owner records check application, and description of services and geographic area (.06(1)). Periodic renewal with a description of services and area (.06(2)). Fees are reasonable and may be refunded for good cause (.06(3)). Applications must be truthful. DCH may refuse a license for false statements (.06(4)).

citations.title: Exemptions
citations.requirement: Rules do not apply to an individual who personally provides services without agents, employees, contractors or financially interested referrals (.07(1)(a)), nor to licensed home health agencies (.07(1)(d)) or personal care home staff (.07(1)(e)). No Certificate of Need is required for a PHCP-only license (.07(2)).

citations.title: Inspections and Plans of Correction
citations.requirement: Periodic inspection, with possible exemption for accredited providers (.08(1)). Application or renewal is consent to entry during regular business hours, and DCH gets access to premises, records, staff and consenting clients (.08(2)). Staff must cooperate without unreasonable delay (.08(3)). An acceptable written plan of correction is due within ten days of receiving the written report. The provider may explain or dispute findings in the plan (.08(4)).

citations.title: Administration and Organization — Services Description
citations.requirement: Written policies and procedures must define the scope of services offered and the types of clients served. No service prohibited by the rules or other law may be provided.

citations.title: Administration and Organization — Service Agreements
citations.requirement: Do not offer services you cannot reasonably deliver. Written policies are required. All services are based on a written agreement with 10 required elements (.09(2)(a)1-10), including referral and contact dates, services, frequency, charges and billing, receipt of rights notice, the provider's phone number, the DCH phone number, authorization for client funds or vehicle use, and signatures. The agreement must be completed by the 2nd visit if on a different day than the 1st, or within 7 calendar days of first service, whichever is earlier (.09(2)(b)). Good-cause delay must be documented (.09(2)(b)1). Later changes are documented in the record as agreed by the client (.09(2)(b)2). The client may cancel at any time and pays only for services rendered. Only a reasonable travel and staff-time charge is allowed if the staff member has already arrived (.09(2)(c)).

citations.title: Administration and Organization — Administrator
citations.requirement: The governing body appoints an administrator with full authority and responsibility for operations. Qualifications: no credible evidence of abuse, neglect, exploitation or deprivation; participation in required orientation and training; no material false statements. The current SOS text of (3)(a)1 also requires a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination. See the notes on version conflict.

citations.title: Record keeping — Client Records
citations.requirement: A separate file per client containing: identifying information; current service agreement; current service plan; signed nursing notes if nursing is provided; documentation of personal care and companion/sitter tasks actually performed; supervisory visit findings; material reports and communications; physician contacts; date and source of referral.

citations.title: Retention and Confidentiality of Client Records
citations.requirement: Written policies must state who supervises records, who has custody, to whom and why records are released, and how long they are retained. Minimum retention is five years from the last service. Disclosure is allowed only to appropriate staff, the client, the responsible party, the client's physician or other provider, DCH, persons authorized in writing by the client, or by subpoena.

citations.title: Personnel Records
citations.requirement: A separate record per employee containing: identifying and emergency contact information; 5-year employment history; qualifications; satisfactory TB screening at hire and annually; date of employment; job description; orientation and training documentation; at least an annual performance evaluation; bonding documentation if the employee has unlimited access to client funds (a universal bond is acceptable).

citations.title: Reports of Complaints and Incidents
citations.requirement: Keep files of all complaints under .12(2). Keep incident reports and reports of unusual occurrences (e.g., falls, accidents, significant medication errors) for at least five years. Documentation must show actions taken to resolve complaints and address incidents.

citations.title: Staffing — General and Nursing Personnel
citations.requirement: Keep sufficient qualified staff for the service agreements. On an unexpected staff shortage, advise the client and refer to another provider if the client wishes. Staff must have a written competency evaluation by direct observation or demonstration. Hires must have no credible evidence of abuse or exploitation, must complete orientation and training, and must make no false qualification statements. Nursing personnel must hold a Georgia license.

citations.title: Personal Care Assistant (PCA) Qualifications
citations.requirement: A PCA must have one of: a nurse aide program under 42 CFR Part 483 Subpart D; a DCH-recognized nurse aide competency exam; a DCH-approved health care or personal care credential; or a 40-hour provider training program covering ambulation and transfer, personal care tasks, first aid and CPR, special conditions, home management, home safety and sanitation, infection control, medically related activities and vital signs, and nutrition. The 40-hour program must be directed by an RN or an equivalent professional. 20 hours must be completed before serving clients and the other 20 within six months of starting. No PCA may be assigned a task without completed training and a competency determination. No PCA may care for a client with special conditions without training and demonstrated competency.

citations.title: Companions or Sitters
citations.requirement: Companions or sitters may perform only companion or sitter tasks unless also qualified as a nurse or PCA. They must read, write, follow instructions and complete reports. They must be trained or competent in the needs of elderly, handicapped or convalescing persons, meal preparation, transport and escort, housekeeping and sanitation, home safety, handling medical emergencies, and infection control.

citations.title: Staff Training
citations.requirement: Orientation before working with clients must cover: written policies on scope of services and client types; client rights and complaints (.12); the employee's duties; reporting client progress and problems and handling medical emergencies and incidents; and the duty to report known exposure to TB or hepatitis. Each employee must receive at least 8 clock hours of training annually after the first year of employment, in subjects relating to their duties.

citations.title: Contracted Services
citations.requirement: Contractor arrangements must be in writing and detail the services. The provider must ensure the contractor follows the rules and is qualified. The services must be supervised under .10(2) by a supervisor of the licensed provider.

citations.title: Categories of Services
citations.requirement: Nursing services are delivered by an RN or LPN under a supervisor. Personal care tasks are performed by a qualified PCA (or nurse) per the service plan. Companion or sitter tasks are performed by a qualified companion or sitter per the service plan. PCAs, companions and sitters must report client needs, changes in condition and observed problems.

citations.title: Supervision of Services; Nursing Supervision
citations.requirement: Qualified staff must supervise all services. Each staff member must be evaluated in writing at least annually by direct observation or demonstration. No supervisor may knowingly permit an employee who has been exposed to or diagnosed with TB or hepatitis to serve clients until the employee is determined not to be contagious. A provider offering nursing must employ a fully licensed Georgia RN supervisor.

citations.title: Supervision of Personal Care Tasks
citations.requirement: Supervisors must be qualified by education, training and experience. A licensed RN or LPN must supervise personal care for medically frail or compromised clients. An RN must complete the initial service plan for those clients. A supervisory home visit to the client's residence is due at least every 92 days from the date of initial service, or sooner as the level of care requires. The visit assesses general condition and vital signs, progress, problems, client satisfaction and appropriateness of services, and is documented in the client file or plan.

citations.title: Supervision of Companion or Sitter Tasks
citations.requirement: A qualified supervisor (RN, LPN, the administrator or another assigned staff member) completes the service plan. A supervisory home visit is due at least every 122 days from initial service, or when a complaint raises a serious question about services. The visit assesses condition, progress, problems, satisfaction and appropriateness of services, is made in the residence, and is documented.

citations.title: On-call Representative for Medically Frail Clients
citations.requirement: When staff perform personal care for medically frail or compromised clients in their homes, a provider representative must be on call and able to reach a nurse supervisor by phone or other means to consult with staff on the clients' medical needs.

citations.title: Documentation of Home Care Services Provided
citations.requirement: Written policies must provide for documenting the services actually performed each day. The documentation goes into the client file under .09(4)(a).

citations.title: Quality Improvement Program
citations.requirement: Maintain documentation of an effective quality improvement program that continuously monitors program performance and client outcomes against standards of care and the rules. At minimum, document receipt and resolution of complaints, problems with care identified, and corrective actions.

citations.title: Service Plans
citations.requirement: Written policies are required. The plan is developed with the client, the responsible party, and the physician if nursing is provided. Content: functional limitations, services, times and frequency, duration, goals and objectives, and discharge plans. Where applicable it also covers diagnoses, medications and treatments, equipment, and diet. The service supervisor completes the plan within seven working days after services start. Nursing plans are reviewed and updated at least every 62 days. Other plans are reviewed at each supervisory visit and revised when the content items change.

citations.title: Client Rights, Responsibilities, and Complaints
citations.requirement: A written notice of rights and responsibilities must be given when the service agreement is completed. It covers 11 items (.12(2)(a)-(k)): participation in planning, being informed of changes, accepting or refusing services, charges, the supervisor's name and contact, complaint procedures and non-retaliation, confidentiality, respect for property and residence, DCH address and phone, a copy of the most recent inspection report on written request (after the plan of correction is filed, with a reasonable copying charge), and the client's duty to report changes in condition. Also required: oral or written complaint procedures with timely resolution (.12(3)), and giving the provider's phone number for information, questions and complaints (.12(4)).

citations.title: Enforcement and Penalties
citations.requirement: After notice and an opportunity for hearing, DCH may refuse, limit, restrict, suspend, revoke or refuse to renew a license, issue a public reprimand, or impose a fine.

citations.title: Rules and Regulations for Criminal Background Checks
citations.requirement: The owner must comply before a new PHCP license is issued (per .05(1)(b)). Which positions beyond the owner and administrator are covered was not verified; confirm with HFRD.

citations.title: In-Home Services
citations.requirement: CCSP in-home service providers must hold a current, valid DCH private home care license.

citations.title: Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver (CCSP/SOURCE)
citations.requirement: 1915(c) waiver approved 11/09/2022 to 11/08/2027. DCH handles reimbursement, enrollment and utilization review, and DAS runs day-to-day CCSP operations.

citations.cite: 21st Century Cures Act (2016) § 12006 — EVV; Georgia DCH EVV program
citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid-financed personal care services. Georgia's system is Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+. Each visit records service type, recipient, provider, date, location and start/end times. Waiver billing: CCSP/SOURCE (IDs 590/930) T1019 with TF/UC; ICWP (660) and NOW/COMP (680/681) T2025.

citations.title: Reporting of need for protective services
citations.requirement: Persons with reasonable cause to believe a disabled adult or elder person has been abused, neglected or exploited must report to the designated adult protection agency (DHS-DAS Adult Protective Services) and to an appropriate law enforcement agency or prosecutor. A staff member of a hospital, social agency, financial institution or similar facility must notify the person in charge, who reports or causes the report. Any other person may report. Good-faith reporters are immune (§ 30-5-4(c)). The statute's list of mandated reporters was seen only in part; the agency's policy treats every caregiver as a reporter.

citations.title: Third-party employers of home care workers
citations.requirement: Per the provided research: third-party employers (agencies) may not claim the companionship exemption from overtime. The 2026 status of this section was not confirmed, so verify before finalizing the overtime policy.

policies.title: Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Owners, members of the governing body, the Administrator, and all supervisory staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To establish who is legally accountable for [AGENCY NAME], to make sure the governing body exercises its authority over all policies and procedures, and to make sure the Administrator is qualified and has full authority to run daily operations in compliance with Georgia Rule 111-8-65.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has a governing body that is empowered and responsible for determining all policies and procedures and for ensuring the agency complies with Rule 111-8-65 (C3). The governing body appoints an Administrator with full authority and responsibility for operations (C10). The Administrator must have no credible evidence of abuse, neglect, sexual assault, exploitation or deprivation, must complete required orientation and training, and must have made no material false statements. As an agency standard, the Administrator must also have a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination, which the current Secretary of State text of the rule requires (C10). The agency operates only under a DCH private home care license or provisional license, and its owners must meet the owner requirements for licensure (C4).

definitions.definition: The person or group with final legal authority over [AGENCY NAME]: the sole proprietor, the general partners, or the board, managers or members of an LLC, association or corporation.

The sole proprietor for a sole proprietorship, the general partners for a partnership, or the entity itself for an LLC, association or corporation. For an entity, its governing body authorizes the application and completes the statement of responsibility (C2).
Any person with a 10% or greater ownership interest who exercises owner authority or operates the business (C2).
The person appointed by the governing body with full authority and responsibility for the agency's operations (C10).
Court, jury, DCH investigation or other reliable evidence that a person committed abuse, neglect, sexual assault, exploitation or deprivation.

procedures: The governing body identifies the licensee type (sole proprietor, partnership, or LLC/association/corporation) and records it in the governing body minutes and the licensing file.
The governing body meets at least quarterly. It records meetings in written minutes kept by [GOVERNING BODY SECRETARY] and approves every policy and procedure in this manual by recorded vote.
The governing body adopts a written resolution appointing [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] as Administrator. The resolution states that the Administrator has full authority and responsibility for operations.

Before the appointment takes effect, the governing body obtains a signed attestation from the Administrator candidate. It states that there is no credible evidence of abuse, neglect, sexual assault, exploitation or deprivation, and that the candidate has made no material false statements to DCH or the agency.

Before the appointment takes effect, the agency completes a fingerprint records check for the Administrator candidate and files the satisfactory determination in the personnel record. An unsatisfactory or pending determination bars appointment (see PER-02).
The Administrator completes all DCH-required orientation and training and files the completion records in the personnel record (see PER-08).

The governing body confirms that every owner (10% or greater interest) has satisfied the owner requirements for licensure before a new license is issued. The Administrator keeps the proof in the licensing file.
The governing body names an alternate administrator or designee in writing, who acts when the Administrator is absent. The designee is listed in the Administrator's delegation letter.

The Administrator reports to the governing body at each quarterly meeting on: client census, complaints, incidents, supervisory visit timeliness, staffing, training status, billing and compliance audits, and inspection results.
The governing body reviews the annual quality improvement report (see GOV-04) and records its decisions and any directed corrective actions in the minutes.

If the Administrator resigns, is terminated, or no longer meets the qualifications, the governing body appoints a qualified replacement as soon as possible. The same day, it names a qualified interim designee and documents the interim designation.
The governing body reviews the Administrator's performance at least annually and documents the evaluation (see PER-09).
The Administrator notifies the governing body within one business day of any DCH inspection, complaint investigation, or enforcement correspondence (see GOV-07).

On any change of agency name, location, ownership or governing body, the governing body directs the Administrator to follow the licensing steps in GOV-02, including returning the license to DCH when required.

responsibilities.duty: Determines all policies, ensures compliance with Rule 111-8-65, appoints and evaluates the Administrator, and keeps minutes.
Has full authority for daily operations, enforces policies, reports to the governing body, and maintains required qualifications and training.
Satisfy licensure requirements for owners and disclose any change in ownership interest to the governing body immediately.
Records and retains minutes, resolutions and the policy approval log.

documentation: Governing body minutes and resolutions
Administrator appointment resolution and delegation or alternate designation letter
Administrator signed attestation, fingerprint records check determination, and orientation and training records
Owner disclosure and licensure compliance records
Annual Administrator evaluation
Organizational chart

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area and Advertising Requirements
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, office staff and anyone who markets or advertises the services of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] never operates without a valid Georgia DCH license, keeps its license and service area information accurate, and advertises only what it is licensed and staffed to deliver.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not provide services until DCH has issued a license or provisional license (C4). Each office location is separately licensed, and the license is displayed at the licensed location. The license is not assignable or transferable, and it is returned to DCH on a change of name, location, ownership or governing body. DCH receives 15 days' advance written notice of a location change (C4). Applications and renewals are truthful and describe the services offered and the geographic area served (C5). Advertising describes only services that are in the application and in the written scope-of-services policy (C8, C20).

definitions.definition: The Georgia DCH private home care provider license that authorizes the agency to operate at one location.
A license that DCH may issue to a new provider for a reasonable but limited time to demonstrate compliance, or to an existing provider with an acceptable plan of improvement (C4).
The geographic area (list of counties) described in the application and renewal (C5).
An exemption for an individual who personally provides services without agents, employees, contractors or financially interested referrals (C6). It does not apply to [AGENCY NAME].

procedures: Before the application is filed, the Administrator confirms in writing that [AGENCY NAME] is not exempt. The agency uses employees, contractors or referral arrangements, so the individual-direct exemption does not apply (C6).

The Administrator confirms that no Certificate of Need is required for a private-home-care-only license (C6). A separate license is required if the agency ever wants to operate as a home health agency or personal care home.

The Administrator prepares the initial application on DCH forms. It includes the application fee, the Board-set license fee, the owner records check applications, and the description of services and geographic area (C5). The governing body reviews and signs it.
The Administrator confirms every statement in the application is accurate and supported by documents before signing. False statements can result in refusal to issue or renew the license (C5).
The Administrator pays all fees as DCH requires. The agency does not begin client services until the license or provisional license is in hand (C4).
Upon receipt, the Administrator posts the license in a visible place at the licensed office at [ADDRESS] and keeps a copy in the licensing file.

If a provisional license is issued, the Administrator calendars the end date and the plan of improvement milestones. The Administrator reports progress to the governing body at each meeting until a full license is issued.

The Administrator keeps a current county list of the service area. The agency does not accept clients outside that list until the application or renewal has been updated and DCH has accepted the change.

The Administrator calendars the renewal due date given by DCH. Because the renewal interval is not stated in the rule, the date on the license or in DCH correspondence controls. Renewal is filed with a current description of services and service area and the required fee (C5).

At least 15 days before any move to a new office location, the Administrator sends DCH written notice and calendars the date. The agency does not operate at the new location until DCH has addressed licensing for that location (C4).
If the agency's name, ownership or governing body changes, the Administrator immediately consults DCH, returns the license as required, and does not operate on the old license (C4).

All advertising, websites, brochures and social media posts are approved in advance by the Administrator. They may describe only services listed in the application and in the scope-of-services policy (GOV-06).
The agency does not advertise nursing services unless it has an RN supervisor employed and has told DCH it provides nursing (C20, see SVC-14).
Advertising identifies the agency as a DCH-licensed private home care provider and does not state or imply services, credentials, or Medicaid program participation the agency does not hold.
The Administrator keeps copies of every advertisement with its first-use date for the licensing file and reviews them at least annually.

responsibilities.duty: Authorizes the application, renewal and any change of location, name or ownership, and ensures the license is never allowed to lapse.
Prepares truthful applications, posts the license, tracks renewal and notice dates, controls the service area list and approves all advertising.
Use only approved materials and refer any question about services outside the scope to the Administrator.

documentation: Application, DCH correspondence and fee receipts
Current license or provisional license and plan of improvement
Renewal calendar
Service area county list with revision dates
15-day location change notice
Advertising file with approval dates

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, supervisors and all employees of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every policy required by Rule 111-8-65 is written, approved by the governing body, kept current, available to staff and surveyors, and actually followed.
policies.policy: The governing body approves every policy and procedure (C3). The agency maintains written, implemented policies on scope of services and client types (C8), service agreements (C9), service planning (C27), and client rights and complaints (C28). It also maintains policies on client record maintenance and security and on daily service documentation. Every policy carries a version date and an approval record. Policies are reviewed at least annually and whenever a rule changes. The agency checks the Georgia Secretary of State rule compilation and DCH public notices every six months, because Rule 111-8-65 had a 2026 revision (public hearing June 16, 2026; final adoption notice July 14, 2026).

definitions.definition: A governing-body-approved statement of what the agency requires, with the procedures staff follow.
The date a policy was last approved or revised, shown on every page.
The signed register listing each policy, its version date and the governing body approval date.

procedures: The Administrator maintains the Policy & Procedure Manual in a master binder or controlled electronic folder at [ADDRESS], and only the Administrator edits the master copy.
Each policy shows its ID, title, version date, and the approval date. The governing body approves each new or revised policy by recorded vote, and the approval is entered in the signed approval log.

The Administrator confirms the manual contains the policies the rule requires: scope of services and client types, service agreements, client record maintenance and security, daily service documentation, service planning, and client rights and complaints (C8, C9, C27, C28). Gaps are corrected before the agency accepts any client.
The Administrator performs a full policy review at least once every 12 months. Each reviewer initials and dates the review, notes any change needed, and the governing body approves the outcome.

Every six months the Administrator checks the Secretary of State rule compilation and DCH public notices for changes to Rule 111-8-65. The Administrator documents the date checked, the version found and any resulting policy action.

When a rule change or DCH direction takes effect, the Administrator drafts conforming revisions within 30 days, or before the effective date if shorter. The Administrator submits them to the governing body for approval.

Revised policies are issued to all employees within 5 business days of approval. Each employee signs an acknowledgment that they received and understand the revision. Training is given when the change affects client care or documentation.
Superseded versions are stamped "SUPERSEDED" with the replacement date and kept in an archive so the agency can show a surveyor which policy applied on any date.

Staff have access to the current manual at the office. Caregivers can request any policy at any time, and the agency gives a copy of the sections affecting their duties during orientation (see PER-03).

The Administrator compares actual practice against policy during the annual self-audit (GOV-04). Where practice differs from policy, the agency either corrects the practice or revises the policy through the governing body. It does not leave a gap.

Forms referenced in policies (service agreement, rights notice, service plan, supervisory visit form) are controlled the same way. Only the current version is used, and the Administrator removes outdated forms from use.
Before a DCH survey, the Administrator confirms the manual, approval log and training acknowledgments are complete and available.

responsibilities.duty: Approves all policies and revisions and records approval in the log.
Controls the master manual, schedules reviews and rule checks, drafts revisions and trains staff.
Report policy gaps or conflicts observed in the field to the Administrator.
Read, acknowledge and follow current policies.

documentation: Master Policy & Procedure Manual with version dates
Signed approval log
Annual review records and six-month rule check log
Archive of superseded policies
Employee acknowledgment and training records for each revision

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, supervisors and any employee who handles complaints, incidents, supervisory visits or records at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To maintain a documented quality improvement program that continuously monitors the agency's performance and client outcomes, finds problems, and shows corrective action, as Rule 111-8-65 requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains documentation of an effective quality improvement program that continuously monitors program performance and client outcomes against standards of care and the rules (C26). At a minimum the program documents the receipt and resolution of client complaints, problems with care that were identified, and the corrective actions taken (C26). The agency keeps complaint files and keeps incident and unusual-occurrence reports (for example falls, accidents and significant medication errors) for at least five years, with documentation of actions taken (C14). The Administrator reports results to the governing body at least quarterly and completes an annual self-audit against Rule 111-8-65.

definitions.definition: The ongoing process of measuring performance and client outcomes, identifying problems, correcting them, and checking that the corrections worked.
An event such as a fall, accident or significant medication error that must be reported internally and filed (C14).
A documented step taken to fix a problem and prevent it from recurring, with an owner and a due date.

procedures: The Administrator is the QI program lead. The governing body approves the annual QI plan listing the indicators to be tracked, who collects the data, and how often.

Every complaint is logged on the complaint log with the date received, the complainant, the issue, the investigator, the action taken and the date resolved (see CR-02). The Administrator reviews the log monthly.
Every incident and unusual occurrence is logged and filed (see SAF-02). The Administrator reviews each for root cause and trends monthly. Records are kept at least five years (C14).

Each month the Administrator tracks supervisory visit timeliness. Visits for clients receiving personal care are due at least every 92 days from the initial service date or sooner if the level of care requires (C22). Visits for clients receiving only companion or sitter services are due at least every 122 days (C23). Any overdue visit is reported to the Administrator, scheduled within 7 days, and recorded on the QI log.

Each month the Administrator audits all new clients for a service agreement signed by the deadline in SVC-02 and CR-06, and for a service plan completed within seven working days of the start of services (SVC-03).

Each quarter the Administrator reviews a sample of at least 10% of active client records, or at least 5 records if fewer than 50 clients. The review checks service plan content, daily documentation against the plan, and evidence that reported changes in condition were acted on.
Each quarter the Administrator verifies that every employee has current TB screening, required training hours, and an annual evaluation on file (see PER-03, PER-04, PER-09).
The agency reviews client outcomes and satisfaction at every supervisory visit. Supervisors record the client's stated satisfaction and any concerns, which feed the QI log.
Each quarter the Administrator reviews missed visits, late visits, hospitalizations, falls, and caregiver turnover for trends and records findings.

When any indicator misses its target or a problem with care is identified, the Administrator writes a corrective action plan with the responsible person and a due date no later than 30 days out. The Administrator verifies completion and re-checks the indicator.

Within 60 days after each calendar year-end, the Administrator completes an annual self-audit against Rule 111-8-65 and presents a written QI report to the governing body. The report covers complaints, problems with care, and corrective actions.
The governing body reviews the QI report, records its decisions in the minutes, and directs any system changes, including policy revisions (see GOV-03).
QI records are kept for at least five years and are available to DCH surveyors on request. Client-identifying information in QI reports is limited to what is needed and protected under CR-03.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the QI plan, reviews reports and directs corrective action.
Leads the QI program, audits indicators, writes corrective action plans and reports to the governing body.
Complete supervisory visits on time, document findings, and report complaints and problems with care promptly.
Report complaints, incidents and care problems immediately and cooperate with QI reviews.

documentation: Annual QI plan and indicator list
Complaint log and incident log with resolution notes
Quarterly record audit tools and results
Corrective action plans with completion verification
Annual self-audit and QI report to the governing body, with minutes

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Owners, governing body, Administrator, billing and scheduling staff, supervisors and all caregivers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To prevent fraud, waste and abuse, to make sure every claim is truthful and supported, and to protect the agency's license and its Medicaid waiver participation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is committed to truthful dealings with DCH, Georgia Medicaid and every client and payer. This policy applies in full to Medicaid waiver billing (CCSP/SOURCE, ICWP and NOW/COMP). For private-pay clients, the same rules on truthfulness and billing only for services delivered apply as agency standards. Applications and renewals submitted to DCH must be truthful (C5). The agency bills only for visits actually delivered and documented. Waiver claims must be supported by electronic visit verification (EVV) and the service plan (C33). A claim for a service that was not performed, or that was performed by unqualified staff, is a false claim. The agency does not pay or receive anything of value for referrals. Waiver in-home providers must hold a current, valid DCH private home care license, and loss of the license ends waiver eligibility (C31, C32).

definitions.definition: A claim for payment that the agency knows, or should know, is false: for services not provided, services provided by unqualified staff, or services not supported by documentation.
Anything of value offered, paid, solicited or received to induce or reward a referral of Medicaid business.
The person designated by the governing body to oversee this policy. For this agency: [COMPLIANCE OFFICER NAME].
Electronic visit verification, required for Medicaid-financed personal care services, using Georgia's system (Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+) (C33).

procedures: The governing body designates [COMPLIANCE OFFICER NAME] as compliance officer. The officer reports directly to the governing body and has authority to stop billing that is in question.

The agency establishes a confidential compliance hotline at [PHONE] and a written reporting option. Staff may report anonymously. The agency prohibits retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith, and violations of this rule are grounds for discipline up to termination.

At hire and annually, each employee and contractor receives training on this policy, including the federal False Claims Act and Medicaid false claims education. The employee signs an acknowledgment, which is filed in the personnel record (see PER-03).

Before any claim is submitted, billing staff verify that the visit has a matching EVV record (service type, recipient, provider, date, location, start and end times) and that the service is in the current service plan and authorization (C33; see SVC-07).
Billing staff verify that the caregiver who delivered the service was qualified and had completed all required checks and training on the date of service (see PER-01 to PER-04).

Billing staff use only the codes for the program: T1019 with the TF/UC modifiers for CCSP/SOURCE, and T2025 for ICWP and NOW/COMP (C33; see SVC-16). Staff do not bill units or hours exceeding the time actually worked.

Claims for any visit lacking EVV, daily documentation or a valid authorization are held. The billing staff member sends the exception to the compliance officer, who decides on correction, adjustment or non-billing and documents the decision.

The agency does not offer or accept payment, gifts or any item of value in exchange for referrals. Referral relationships are reviewed by the compliance officer before being entered into, and any financially interested referral arrangement is evaluated for licensure and legal implications.

The compliance officer screens all employees and contractors against federal and state exclusion lists before hire and at least monthly thereafter (see PER-02). Any excluded individual is removed from billable work immediately.
Each quarter the compliance officer audits a sample of paid claims against EVV records, daily notes and service plans, and records findings and corrective actions.

If an overpayment or billing error is found, the compliance officer stops affected billing, quantifies the error, and refunds or corrects it with the payer promptly. The governing body is told at its next meeting, and the officer consults legal counsel where needed.

All statements to DCH, DHS Division of Aging Services, DBHDD and payers, including applications, renewals, cost or enrollment reports and attestations, are reviewed for accuracy and signed only by the Administrator or an authorized owner (C5).
The compliance officer investigates every report within 10 business days. The officer documents what was found, what was done, and who was told, and reports to the governing body at least quarterly.

The agency keeps the DCH license current at all times, because waiver participation depends on it (C31). The Administrator notifies the compliance officer and governing body immediately if any license issue or enforcement action arises (see GOV-07).

responsibilities.duty: Designates the compliance officer, supports the hotline, enforces the non-retaliation rule and reviews compliance reports.
Trains staff, runs audits and exclusion screening, investigates reports and manages corrections and refunds.
Bill only supported, verified claims and escalate exceptions.
Record time and services truthfully, and report suspected fraud or billing problems.

documentation: Compliance officer designation and hotline notice
Training records and signed acknowledgments
Exclusion screening log
Quarterly claims audit reports
Compliance investigations, corrections and refund records
Governing body compliance reports

policies.title: Services Description and Types of Clients Served
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, intake staff, supervisors and all caregivers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define in writing the private home care services [AGENCY NAME] offers and the clients it serves, so that no service is provided that the rules prohibit or that the agency cannot reasonably deliver.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has written policies defining the scope of the services it offers and the types of clients it serves (C8). No service prohibited by the rules or other law is provided. The agency offers only the categories of service listed in the current application. Personal care tasks are performed only by a qualified personal care aide (PCA) or nurse under the service plan. Companion or sitter tasks are performed only by a qualified companion or sitter under the service plan. Nursing services are delivered only by an RN or LPN under a supervisor (C20). Caregivers report client needs, changes in condition and observed problems (C20). The agency does not accept a client whose needs exceed the agency's scope or its trained staff's competencies.

definitions.definition: Tasks defined by the rule, including bathing, toileting, grooming, shaving, dental care, dressing and eating, along with related nutrition, home management, housekeeping, ambulation and transfer, and medically related activities. Vital signs are taken only in connection with these tasks (C2).
Tasks defined by the rule, including transport and escort, meal preparation and serving, and household tasks essential to cleanliness and safety (C2).
Services performed only by a licensed RN or LPN. Offered only if the agency has elected this category (see SVC-14).
Reminding clients to take medication and assisting with self-administration, excluding professional services (C2).

The client's home: the client's own home, a friend's or relative's home, or a personal care home. Hospitals, nursing homes, hospices and similar licensed facilities are not a residence under the rule.

definitions.term: Services excluded from private home care services
definitions.definition: Physical, speech and occupational therapy, medical nutrition therapy, medical social services, home health aide services of a licensed home health agency, and proxy caregiver services hired by the patient (C2).

procedures: The governing body decides which categories of service the agency will offer (personal care, companion or sitter, nursing) and records the decision in the minutes. The categories must match the license application (C8; see GOV-02).

The Administrator maintains a one-page services and client types statement approved by the governing body. It lists each service offered, the clients served and the counties covered. It is attached to this policy and updated whenever the offering changes.

The statement describes the types of clients served: adults and others who live in their own residence and need personal care, companion or sitter services, or, if offered, nursing. It also states the waiver programs the agency is enrolled in: CCSP/SOURCE, ICWP and NOW/COMP, as applicable.

The Administrator confirms that clients live in a residence as the rule defines it. The agency does not provide private home care services in a hospital, nursing home, hospice or similar licensed facility.

The agency does not provide therapies, medical nutrition therapy, medical social services, home health aide services of a licensed home health agency, or proxy caregiver services. Staff direct any such request to the Administrator, who refers the client to an appropriate licensed provider.

Before accepting any referral, intake staff confirm with a supervisor that the requested services are within the scope of services and that staff with the right qualifications and training are available (see SVC-02). The agency does not offer services it cannot reasonably deliver.

If a client's assessed needs exceed the scope or the competencies of trained staff, the supervisor documents the reason, declines or discontinues in accordance with SVC-09, and helps the client find an appropriate provider.
Clients who are medically frail or medically compromised are served only under RN or LPN supervision as set out in SVC-13.

Every employee is told the scope of services and the client types served during orientation, and each caregiver receives the task list matching their qualification (see PER-03, SVC-01). Caregivers sign that they understand which tasks they may and may not perform.

Caregivers must not perform any task outside their qualification category or the client's service plan, even at the client's or family's request. They report the request to the supervisor, who addresses it with the client.
Caregivers report client needs, changes in condition and observed problems to the supervisor the same day, or immediately in an emergency (see SVC-08).

The Administrator reviews the services and client types statement annually and when asked to add a service. Before a new service is offered, the Administrator confirms that the rule allows it, that qualified staff are hired and trained, and that DCH has been informed as needed.
The agency's marketing materials, service agreements and rights notices describe only the services in the current statement (see CR-06).

responsibilities.duty: Decides and approves the scope of services and types of clients served.
Maintains the services and client types statement, screens requests for new services, and ensures staff capacity.
Apply the scope in accepting clients and writing service plans.
Perform only tasks within their qualification and the service plan, and report needs and changes.

documentation: Governing body decision on services offered
Services and client types statement with revision dates
Intake screening records showing scope and staffing review
Caregiver acknowledgment of task scope in the personnel record
Referral-out and declined-referral records

policies.title: DCH Inspections, Plans of Correction and Enforcement
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervisors, all office staff and caregivers; all service lines under the Private Home Care Provider (PHCP) license
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] cooperates fully with Georgia DCH Healthcare Facility Regulation Division (HFRD) inspections, files an acceptable plan of correction on time, and responds appropriately to any enforcement action.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] consents to DCH inspection as a condition of its license application and renewal. DCH may inspect during regular business hours and may inspect whenever it decides it is necessary. We give DCH reasonable and meaningful access to our premises, licensure-related records, all staff and consenting clients. Staff cooperate and produce documents without unreasonable delay (C7). We file a written plan of correction within TEN days of RECEIVING the written inspection report, and we use that plan to explain or dispute findings when appropriate (C7). We never retaliate against any client or employee who speaks with DCH. DCH may refuse, limit, restrict, suspend, revoke or refuse to renew a license, issue a public reprimand or impose a fine, after notice and an opportunity for hearing (C29). Clients may obtain the most recent completed inspection report on written request, as described in their notice of rights (C28).

definitions.definition: Any DCH survey, monitoring visit or complaint investigation of the agency, whether announced or unannounced.
A written document stating, for each cited violation, what the agency will do to correct it and by when. It may also explain or dispute a finding.
The day the written inspection report actually arrives at the agency by mail, email, portal or hand delivery. The ten-day POC clock runs from this date.
DCH may exempt a provider that is certified or accredited by a DCH-recognized body in place of its own inspection. The provider must submit its most recent accreditation report.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) is the agency's inspection contact. The Administrator names a trained alternate ([ALTERNATE NAME]) who acts when the Administrator is unavailable. Both names and phone numbers are posted at the front desk and given to all office staff.
Keep the current DCH license posted at the office ([ADDRESS]) and keep licensure records organized and retrievable at the office during regular business hours of [BUSINESS HOURS].

When anyone identifying themselves as a DCH representative arrives, the first staff member contacted checks identification, notifies the Administrator or alternate at once, and starts an Inspection Log with the arrival time and the names and titles of the inspectors.
Do not delay or turn away inspectors. The Administrator or alternate gives them access to the premises, licensure-related records and staff without unreasonable delay.
Staff produce requested records promptly. The Administrator keeps a log of every document copied or handed over. Disclosure of client records to DCH is permitted; see CR-03 for the access log.

If inspectors ask to speak with clients, the agency helps arrange contact only with clients who consent. Staff do not coach, discourage or screen client responses and do not ask clients afterward what they said.
Staff answer inspector questions truthfully and directly. Staff never alter, backdate or create records after the inspection starts.
The Administrator attends the exit conference, takes written notes of each preliminary finding and asks for clarification of any regulation cited.

Designate one person ([REPORT RECEIPT DESIGNEE]) to receive DCH mail and email. That person date-stamps and logs the written report on the day it arrives and gives it to the Administrator the same day.

On the day of receipt, the Administrator calculates the due date (ten days after receipt) and enters it on the compliance calendar. The Administrator also sends the report to the governing body (see GOV-01).

Within three business days of receipt, the Administrator and supervisors review each cited violation. They identify the root cause, the corrective action, the person responsible and a completion date for each.
The Administrator drafts the POC. For each violation it states what will be done and when. If the agency disagrees with a finding, the POC explains or disputes it with supporting facts.

The Administrator submits the signed POC to DCH on or before the due date by a traceable method (portal confirmation, certified mail or email read receipt). A copy of the POC and the proof of delivery go in the inspection file.
If DCH finds the POC unacceptable, the Administrator revises it promptly and resubmits it as DCH directs.

The Administrator implements each corrective action by the date promised, verifies completion, and documents it. Quality Assurance (GOV-04) monitors the cited areas for at least three months to confirm the correction holds.

When a client asks in writing for the most recent inspection report, the Administrator may hold the request until the POC has been filed, then provides a copy. The agency may charge a reasonable copying fee, which is disclosed to the client. See CR-07.
If the agency is accredited by a DCH-recognized body, the Administrator submits the most recent accreditation report when DCH requests it to support an exemption. DCH decides whether to grant it.

If DCH issues notice of a proposed enforcement action (reprimand, limit, restriction, suspension, fine, revocation or non-renewal), the Administrator informs the governing body the same day and consults legal counsel. The Administrator calendars the deadline in the notice for requesting a hearing, and files the request on time if the agency contests the action.

If a license restriction or suspension affects services, the Administrator follows SVC-09 and SVC-12 so clients receive notice and are helped to find other providers, and continues to serve clients safely while the agency remains authorized to operate.

responsibilities.duty: Serve as inspection contact, receive inspectors, calendar and meet the ten-day POC deadline, sign and submit the POC, brief the governing body, and manage any enforcement response.
Act as inspection contact when the Administrator is unavailable.
Log DCH correspondence the day it arrives and deliver it to the Administrator immediately.
Cooperate with inspectors, produce records without delay, and never obstruct or retaliate.
Review each inspection report and POC and the status of corrective actions.
Monitor corrected areas after the inspection and report results under GOV-04.

documentation: Inspection Log (arrival time, inspector names, documents provided, interviews)
Exit conference notes
Written inspection report with date-of-receipt stamp
Compliance calendar entry showing the POC due date
Root-cause worksheet and signed POC with proof of submission
Evidence of completion of each corrective action
Post-inspection monitoring records
Any enforcement notice, hearing request and correspondence
Client requests for inspection reports and the date each was fulfilled

policies.title: Contracted Services and Worker Classification
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervisors, human resources and anyone who engages a contractor, individual or agent to deliver services
policies.purpose: To ensure that any person engaged by [AGENCY NAME] other than as a regular employee is properly classified, qualified, covered by a written agreement, and supervised to the same standard as employees.
policies.policy: The default practice of [AGENCY NAME] is to engage personal care aides and companion/sitters as W-2 employees. The agency uses an independent contractor only where it has made a documented classification determination and a written contract is in place. Every contractor arrangement is in writing and details the services to be provided. The Administrator ensures each contractor follows Rule 111-8-65 and is qualified for the work. A supervisor of [AGENCY NAME] supervises contracted services in the same way and at the same frequency as employee services (C19). Because individuals who work for the agency as agents, employees or contractors are within the licensure framework (C6), the agency does not use contracting to avoid its licensure, training, background check or supervision duties. The agency also does not refer a caregiver to a client where it, or anyone with an ownership or financial interest in it, would profit from delivering that service without first being properly licensed.

definitions.definition: A person or business engaged by the agency under a written agreement to provide services to clients, without being the agency's employee.

A person or entity that offers nursing, personal care or companion/sitter services in a client's residence, with the licensing definition's coverage of employees, agents and, in defined circumstances, contractors and financially interested referrals.
The determination of whether a worker is an employee or an independent contractor under federal and state law.
A visit to the client's residence by a qualified supervisor of the agency to assess condition, progress, problems, satisfaction and appropriateness of services.

procedures: Treat all personal care aides and companion/sitters as W-2 employees unless the Administrator documents a different classification decision with the reasons.

Before engaging any contractor, the Administrator completes a Worker Classification Checklist applying the Department of Labor economic reality factors referenced in 29 CFR Part 552 and any applicable state tests. The Administrator signs and dates the checklist and files it. If the answer is unclear, the worker is treated as an employee.

Under the licensing definition, independent contractors are covered only where they are health care professionals licensed under Title 43. The Administrator limits any contracting for client services to licensed professionals (such as a licensed nurse or therapist) and verifies the license on the Georgia licensing board's website before engagement.

Prepare a written contract before any services begin. It must identify the parties, describe the services in detail, state rates and billing method, require compliance with Rule 111-8-65, and describe the agency's supervision of the services.

The contract must also require the contractor to meet the agency's background check, TB screening, orientation, competency and training requirements for the role. It must state the contractor's duties to report abuse, neglect, exploitation, incidents and changes in client condition to the agency immediately.

Before assignment, verify the contractor's qualifications (license, credentials, references) and complete the background check and registry checks under PER-02. File the verification in the contractor file.
Verify that contractors who will handle client funds are bonded under CR-04 and the service agreement authorizes it.
Orient contractors on agency policies, client rights, abuse reporting, infection control and documentation before their first client contact (PER-03).

Assign each contractor to a named agency supervisor who completes the service plan and makes supervisory home visits to contracted clients at least every 122 days, or sooner if the payer, service plan or a complaint requires.
Contractors document services on the agency's forms or EVV system (SVC-07, SVC-11) so the agency has a complete record of every visit.
The Administrator reviews each contract at least annually and at renewal, and documents whether the contractor continues to meet qualifications and the services remain supervised.

Do not refer or place a caregiver with a client when the agency or any owner or other person with a financial interest in the referral would profit from the service, unless that arrangement is covered by the agency's license and the client service agreement.
If a contractor violates the contract or agency policy, the Administrator takes corrective action, up to termination, and notifies the client and payer as required.
The Administrator monitors changes in DCH rules and U.S. Department of Labor regulations on classification and updates this policy through GOV-03.
Report the status of all contracts to the governing body at least annually (GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Approve classifications and contracts, verify qualifications, ensure supervision, and conduct the annual contract review.
Supervise contracted services including visits at least every 122 days and document findings.
Maintain classification checklists, contract files, background check records and license verifications.
Follow the contract, agency policies and Rule 111-8-65, document each visit and report incidents and abuse promptly.
Review contracted arrangements at least annually.

documentation: Worker Classification Checklist signed and dated
Written contract with detailed description of services
Verification of professional license and credentials
Background and registry check results
Orientation and competency records for contractors
Supervisory visit records for contracted clients
Annual contract review notes

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All clients and responsible parties; intake staff, supervisors, caregivers
policies.purpose: To ensure every client or responsible party receives and understands a written notice of rights and responsibilities and that [AGENCY NAME] honors those rights in daily service delivery.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] gives each client or responsible party a written notice of rights and responsibilities when the service agreement is completed (C28). The service agreement contains an acknowledgment that the client received the notice (C9). The notice contains all eleven required items: (a) the right to be informed about and participate in the plan of service; (b) to be promptly and fully informed of plan changes; (c) to accept or refuse services; (d) to be informed of charges; (e) the name, business phone and address of the supervisor and how to reach that person; (f) complaint procedures, the right to complain without fear of discrimination or retaliation, investigation within a reasonable time, and the name, address and phone of the person handling complaints; (g) confidentiality of the record; (h) respect for property and residence; (i) written notice of the DCH address and phone and a statement that DCH licenses the agency and investigates complaints that appear to violate licensing rules; (j) a copy of the most recent licensure inspection report on written request; and (k) the client's and responsible party's duty to tell the agency about changes in condition or events affecting service needs (C28). Clients who receive Medicaid waiver services also receive the program's own rights and appeal information.

definitions.definition: A person authorized in writing by the client or appointed by a court, including a family member of an impaired client who cannot authorize services.
The written document listing the eleven required items that is given to the client when the service agreement is completed.

The written agreement for services required by the licensure rule, completed by the second visit if on a different day than the first, or within 7 calendar days of the first service, whichever is earlier.
A client receiving services under CCSP/SOURCE, ICWP or NOW/COMP.

procedures: Use the agency's current Notice of Client Rights and Responsibilities form, approved by the Administrator and reviewed under GOV-03. The form must contain all eleven required items.

The intake staff member or supervisor reviews the notice in person with the client or responsible party during the in-home visit when the service agreement is completed, and no later than the deadline for completing the agreement.
Present the notice in plain language and in the client's preferred language or format (CR-05). Read it aloud to clients who cannot read it and offer time for questions.

Insert the name, business phone and address of the assigned supervisor, the complaint handler's name, address and phone, and the DCH address and phone before it is given to the client. Never give a notice with blanks.
Explain that DCH licenses the agency and investigates complaints that appear to violate licensing rules, and give the DCH address and phone number in writing.
Explain the right to accept or refuse services and that refusing a service does not mean the client will be treated badly. Document any refusal in the daily record and notify the supervisor.
