A person designated under PER-08 who meets the agency's qualifications to supervise the type of service being evaluated.

procedures: The HR/Personnel Coordinator keeps a evaluation due-date tracker for every employee, based on the date of hire and the date of the last evaluation.
Sixty days before each due date, the Coordinator gives the responsible supervisor a list of employees due, with the client assignments that make observation possible.

The supervisor pulls the employee's job description and the list of ALL required tasks for the position, including tasks in the personal care, companion/sitter and, where applicable, nursing categories.

The supervisor schedules the observation with the client's agreement, and tells the client the visit is for staff evaluation. The client may decline observation, in which case the supervisor chooses another client or uses a demonstration.

The supervisor observes the employee in the client's home performing the required tasks. Tasks that cannot be seen during the visit, such as an unusual transfer or a task not needed by that client, are covered by a demonstration with the supervisor.

The supervisor completes the Competency Observation Checklist during or immediately after the visit. For each required task the checklist records the task, whether it was observed or demonstrated, the date, the result (competent or needs improvement) and comments.

The supervisor completes the written annual Performance Evaluation form. It covers work quality, following the service plan, documentation, reliability, professional boundaries (PER-07), client feedback, and any complaints or incidents involving the employee.
The supervisor reviews the evaluation with the employee, who signs and dates it. If the employee refuses to sign, the supervisor notes the refusal on the form.

If any task is rated 'needs improvement', the supervisor writes a retraining plan with a target date, provides the retraining, and repeats the observation or demonstration of that task. The employee is not assigned to perform that task unsupervised until competence is documented.
Retraining and re-evaluation results are recorded on the same checklist or an attached addendum, with date and supervisor signature.

If a gap raises a client safety concern, the supervisor notifies [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] immediately. The Administrator decides whether the employee is removed from the task or from the schedule pending retraining, and whether SAF-02 incident reporting applies.
Within five business days of the evaluation, the supervisor gives the completed evaluation and checklists to the Coordinator, who files them in the employee's personnel record (PER-05).
The Coordinator updates the tracker and flags any employee more than 10 days past due to the Administrator weekly until the evaluation is completed.
The Administrator reviews evaluation completion rates and common competency gaps at each quality review (GOV-04) and uses them to update orientation and in-service training (PER-03).
Supervisors are themselves evaluated annually by the Administrator or the Administrator's designee, with the evaluation documented in the supervisor's personnel record.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure every employee is evaluated on time, decides on removal from tasks when safety is at risk, and reviews results for quality improvement.
Observes employees, completes the checklist and evaluation, delivers retraining, and re-evaluates until competence is shown.
Maintains the due-date tracker, notifies supervisors, files completed evaluations, and reports overdue items.
Takes part in observations and demonstrations, signs the evaluation, and completes any assigned retraining.

documentation: Signed and dated annual Performance Evaluation in each personnel record
Competency Observation Checklist listing every required task, the method (observation or demonstration), the date and the result
Retraining plans and re-evaluation results
Evaluation due-date tracker and overdue reports
Quality review minutes that summarize evaluation findings

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff who create, use, store or have custody of client records, and the Administrator, who supervises records.
federal: 45 CFR 164.316(b)(2) and 164.530(j) (HIPAA documentation retention, six years, for policies and related documentation)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, accurate and secure file for each client, that it documents the services actually performed, and that records are kept for the required time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps one separate file for each client. The file holds the items the Georgia private home care rules require, including documentation of the personal care and companion/sitter tasks actually performed each day. Client records are kept for at least FIVE YEARS from the date of the client's last service. If a payer or waiver program requires a longer period, the longer period applies. The Administrator supervises the records system and [RECORDS CUSTODIAN NAME/TITLE] has custody of the files. Records are released only as described in REC-04. Records are stored securely, backed up, and destroyed only after the retention period, with a destruction log. HIPAA-required policies and related documentation are kept for six years.

definitions.definition: The separate file kept for each client, in paper, electronic or both forms, containing the required contents listed in this policy.
The last date on which [AGENCY NAME] provided a service to the client. The retention period runs from this date.
The person designated by the Administrator to hold, control access to, and retrieve client records.
The person who acts for the client in dealings with the agency, such as a legal representative or family member named in the service agreement.

procedures: At intake, the Intake Coordinator opens a separate file for the client, whether paper or electronic, and records the client's name, address and phone number, and the name and contact information of any responsible party.
The Intake Coordinator records the date and source of referral in the file at intake.
The Intake Coordinator records the name, address and phone number of each of the client's physicians and other relevant providers as they are identified.
When the service agreement is signed, the signed copy is placed in the file. Superseded agreements are retained and marked with the date they ended.
When the service plan is completed and each time it is updated, the current plan is placed in the file and prior versions are retained (SVC-03).
If nursing services are provided, the nurse signs and dates each nursing note and files it in the client record.

Each caregiver documents on the daily service record the personal care or companion/sitter tasks actually performed at each visit, as required by SVC-11. The records are placed in the client file at least weekly.
The supervisor files supervisory visit findings in the client record, unless the findings are recorded within the service plan (SVC-04).

Staff file material reports and communications about the client, such as changes in condition, family or physician calls and incident reports, in the record on the day received or the next business day.
The record custodian reviews each active file quarterly against the required-contents checklist, and corrects missing items within 14 days.

Electronic records are protected by individual passwords and role-based access, and are backed up at least daily [CONFIRM FREQUENCY]. Paper records are kept in a locked cabinet in a locked office, with a sign-out log for any file removed.
Staff may not take records off site except for client visits that require them, and never leave records unattended in a vehicle.

When a client is discharged, the record custodian marks the date of last service, closes the file, and calculates the earliest destruction date: five years from the last service, or longer if a payer or waiver requirement applies.
The Administrator confirms the longer retention periods in the Medicaid provider agreement and waiver program requirements, and records the period that applies in the retention schedule.

After the retention period ends, the record custodian, with the Administrator's written approval, destroys the records by shredding or secure electronic deletion, and enters the client identifier, destruction date, method and staff name in the destruction log.
Records that are subject to a pending inspection, complaint, investigation, audit or subpoena are not destroyed until the Administrator releases the hold in writing.

responsibilities.duty: Supervises the records system, approves retention exceptions and destruction, and handles record holds.
Holds the files, controls access, performs quarterly reviews, closes files, and keeps the destruction log.
Opens the file and records identifying information, referral, physician and agreement information.
Files supervisory visit findings, service plan updates and signed nursing notes.
Documents tasks actually performed at every visit, accurately and on the same day.

documentation: Client file with the required contents checklist
Quarterly record review checklist
Record sign-out log
Retention schedule showing the retention period that applies to each program
Destruction log with approvals
Record hold notices and releases
HIPAA policies and related documentation, kept six years

policies.title: Required Reports and Notices to the State
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, supervisors and any staff who prepare or submit notices, applications, plans of correction, claims or abuse reports.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] makes every required report, notice and submission to the Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH), Adult Protective Services, Medicaid and waiver programs accurately and on time.
policies.policy: Rule 111-8-65 does not require a routine periodic report to DCH. [AGENCY NAME] nevertheless meets every notice and submission the rule and related laws require: the renewal application; 15 days' advance notice of a change of location; return of the license on a change of name, location, ownership or governing body; a written plan of correction within ten days of receiving an inspection report; accreditation documents if the agency seeks an inspection exemption; reports of suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult; and Medicaid EVV data, claims and waiver case manager notifications. All applications and submissions are truthful. Each notice is calendared, sent by a traceable method, and a copy kept in the compliance file.

definitions.definition: A written plan submitted to DCH that states how and when the agency will correct each finding in an inspection report. It may also explain or dispute findings.
Any move of the licensed office. Each location is separately licensed.
Adult Protective Services, the Georgia DHS Division of Aging Services program that receives reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of disabled adults and elders.
Electronic Visit Verification, the Georgia Medicaid system (Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+) that records service type, client, provider, date, location and start and end times of each visit.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a compliance calendar listing the license expiration and renewal dates, the DCH-set renewal deadline, and the dates of any open plans of correction.
At least 90 days before the license expires, or sooner if DCH sets an earlier date, the Administrator obtains the DCH renewal forms and fee amount from the DCH Private Home Care Program.

The Administrator completes the renewal application with an accurate description of the services offered and the geographic area served, makes sure no statement is false, attaches the Board-set renewal fee, and sends it by a traceable method on or before the date DCH sets.
Before any planned move of the office, the Administrator sends written notice to DCH at least 15 days BEFORE the move, by a traceable method, and keeps a copy in the compliance file.

On any change of name, location, ownership or governing body, the Administrator returns the license to DCH. The license is not assignable or transferable. The Administrator also confirms with DCH what new application or license is required before operating under the new name, location, owner or governing body.
The Administrator keeps the license displayed at the office, and confirms the posted license matches the current name, location and ownership.
On receiving an inspection report, the Administrator date-stamps it, and immediately calendars the tenth day after receipt as the plan of correction deadline (GOV-07).

The Administrator drafts the plan of correction with the supervisors, states the corrective action, responsible person and completion date for each finding, and includes any explanation or dispute of a finding.
The Administrator submits the plan of correction to DCH within ten days of receipt, by a traceable method, and keeps proof of delivery.
If the agency seeks an inspection exemption based on accreditation, the Administrator sends the accreditation documentation to DCH and keeps a copy in the compliance file.

Any caregiver or staff member who has reasonable cause to believe a client has been abused, neglected or exploited reports immediately to the Administrator or supervisor, and the agency makes the report to Adult Protective Services (1-866-552-4464, press 3) and to the appropriate law enforcement agency, as provided in SAF-01. The agency treats every caregiver as a reporter. Staff may also report directly, and good-faith reporters are protected.
The Administrator records each abuse report in the incident file with date, time, agency contacted, name of the person who took the report and any reference number (REC-03).
The Billing Manager makes sure each visit billed to Medicaid is captured through EVV, and that claims are submitted in GAMMIS using the correct waiver code (SVC-07, SVC-16).
The Care Coordinator notifies the waiver case manager of changes in condition, hospitalizations, missed visits, critical incidents and discharge as required for each program (SVC-10, SAF-08).

The DCH Private Home Care Program telephone numbers listed on DCH pages vary, for example (404) 657-9975 and (404) 657-5700. The Administrator confirms the current number with DCH before relying on it and records the confirmed number [DCH HFRD PHONE] in the compliance file.
The Administrator reviews the compliance calendar monthly, and reports any missed or at-risk deadlines to the governing body at the next meeting (GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Owns the compliance calendar, renewal, location and ownership notices, plans of correction, and the abuse reporting process.
Receives reports on compliance deadlines, approves changes of name, ownership and location, and makes sure the Administrator has the resources to comply.
Makes sure EVV data and Medicaid claims are submitted accurately and on time.
Make waiver case manager notifications and escalate abuse concerns to the Administrator without delay.
Report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately.

documentation: Compliance calendar
Renewal application and proof of fee payment and submission
15-day location change notice and proof of delivery
License return documentation on a change of name, location, ownership or governing body
Inspection report, plan of correction and proof of submission within ten days
Accreditation documents submitted to DCH, if any
APS and law enforcement report records
EVV and claim submission reports
Waiver case manager notification log

policies.title: Complaint and Incident Files
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, supervisors, and all staff who receive complaints or complete incident reports.
policies.purpose: To make sure every client complaint, incident and unusual occurrence is recorded, resolved or addressed, and kept for at least five years, with documentation of the action taken.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a file of all documentation of complaints submitted under the client rights and complaints procedure. It also keeps incident reports and reports of unusual occurrences, such as falls, accidents and significant medication errors, for at least five years. Each file shows the actions the agency took to resolve the complaint or address the incident. Complaints and incidents are recorded in a numbered log that is reviewed quarterly as part of the agency's quality improvement review. Complaint and incident files are confidential and are kept separately from, but cross-referenced to, the client record.

definitions.definition: Any oral or written expression of dissatisfaction or concern about the agency, its services or its staff, from a client, a responsible party or anyone else.

An event that affects or could affect the health, safety or rights of a client or staff member, such as a fall, accident, injury, significant medication error, missed visit with harm or suspected abuse.
The numbered register of complaints and incidents with date received, source, summary, investigator, findings, action and closure date.

procedures: Any employee who receives a complaint, oral or written, records it the same day on the Complaint Form and gives it to the Administrator or supervisor within one business day.
Any employee who witnesses or learns of an incident or unusual occurrence completes the Incident Report the same day, and notifies the supervisor immediately if a client needs help (SAF-02).
The Administrator assigns the next number in the log and enters the date received, source (client, family, staff, other), summary, and the name of the investigator.
The investigator contacts the complainant or client promptly, tells them the matter is being looked into, and gives them the agency phone number for questions and complaints.
The investigator interviews those involved, reviews the client record and schedule, and writes the findings in the file.
The Administrator decides on corrective action, such as retraining, supervision, a service plan change, or discipline, and records it with the responsible person and date.
The agency tells the complainant the outcome in writing or orally, and records the date and method of that contact. This is done in a timely way, as set out in CR-02.

If the matter involves suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, a critical incident reportable for a waiver client, or a Medicaid billing concern, the Administrator also follows SAF-01, SAF-08 or GOV-05 and attaches proof of those reports to the file.
The Administrator closes the file when the resolution or corrective action is complete, records the closure date in the log, and signs the file.
A complainant is never retaliated against. Any report of retaliation is recorded as a new complaint.
Completed files are kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic folder, separate from personnel files. A cross-reference note is placed in the client record.

Complaint and incident files are kept for at least five years from the date of closure. The Administrator confirms the retention period for each file, and does not destroy files subject to an inspection, investigation or litigation hold.

Each quarter the Administrator summarizes the log by type, location, staff and trend, and presents it to the quality improvement review (GOV-04). Actions taken on the trends are recorded in the minutes.
When DCH asks to see complaint and incident files during an inspection, the Administrator provides the files without unreasonable delay.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the complaint and incident log, assigns investigators, decides on corrective action, closes files, and presents quarterly summaries.
Receives reports from caregivers, investigates assigned matters, and documents findings and actions.
Record and report complaints and incidents the same day, and cooperate with investigations.
Stores the files securely and applies retention rules.

documentation: Complaint Form and Incident Report
Numbered complaint and incident log
Investigation notes and findings
Record of corrective action and resolution, with dates
Notice of outcome to the complainant
Quarterly log summary and quality improvement minutes
Retention and destruction records

policies.title: Release of Information, Subpoenas and Record Access
policies.applies_to: All staff, and particularly the Administrator and Record Custodian, who receive requests for information from clients, other providers, family members, DCH, attorneys, courts or anyone else.
policies.purpose: To control who may see or receive client information, to meet the Georgia confidentiality rule and HIPAA, and to make sure DCH and clients can get the access they are entitled to.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] discloses client record information only to: appropriate agency staff; the client; the responsible party; the client's physician or other health care provider; DCH; persons the client has authorized in writing; or in response to a subpoena. Any other release requires a written, signed and dated authorization from the client or the client's legal representative. Every disclosure other than routine use by staff is logged. DCH is given reasonable and meaningful access to records relevant to licensure, and staff provide the documents without unreasonable delay. Clients have the right to see and obtain a copy of their records. Subpoenas go to the Administrator. This policy is applied together with CR-03 on privacy and HIPAA.

definitions.definition: A written, signed and dated document in which the client or legal representative permits release of specific information to a named person or organization for a stated purpose.
A written order from a court or authorized party requiring the production of records or testimony.
The person who acts for the client and is named in the service agreement or documented as the client's legal representative.

procedures: Any employee who receives a request for client information, from any person, refers it to the Record Custodian or Administrator and does not release anything unless this policy clearly permits it.
The Record Custodian verifies the identity of the requester and the requester's authority, for example by checking identification, the service agreement, or a callback to a number on file.

For a request from the client or the responsible party, the Record Custodian provides access to the record, or a copy, and responds within 30 days of the request where HIPAA applies, as required by HIPAA. The Administrator reviews any denial or partial access before it is communicated.
For a request from the client's physician or another health care provider involved in the client's care, the Record Custodian releases only the information needed for that care and logs the release.

For any other request, such as from an insurer, attorney, relative who is not the responsible party, employer or media, the Record Custodian obtains a written, signed and dated authorization naming the recipient, the information and the purpose, before releasing anything.
The Record Custodian checks that the authorization is complete and not expired or revoked, files it in the client record, and releases only what it covers.
A client may revoke an authorization in writing at any time. The Record Custodian notes the revocation in the file and stops further release from that date.

For DCH, when the Administrator receives notice of an inspection or investigation, the Administrator makes sure DCH inspectors are given access to premises, records, staff and consenting clients during regular business hours. Staff provide requested documents without unreasonable delay, and the Administrator keeps a list of what was provided.

For client access to records that are relevant to a licensure inspection, only DCH and consenting clients are involved. Other staff are told that cooperation is required, and that no retaliation will occur against any client who talks with DCH.
If staff receive a subpoena, they do not release anything but give the subpoena to the Administrator on the same day. The Administrator logs the date and time received.

The Administrator confirms the subpoena is valid and properly served, identifies exactly which records are requested, and obtains legal advice before producing records or objecting. The Administrator also notifies the client when appropriate, as legal advice directs.
The Administrator produces only the records the subpoena covers, by the date required, with a copy kept of everything produced and a record of who received it.

The Record Custodian enters every disclosure that is not routine staff use in the Disclosure Log, with date, recipient, what was released, the legal basis (client request, provider care, DCH, authorization or subpoena) and the staff member who released it.

Copy charges, where made, are limited to reasonable cost and are explained to the requester in advance. A client is not refused access for inability to pay a copying charge without Administrator review.
Any release that violates this policy is reported to the Administrator the same day and handled under CR-03 as a possible privacy incident.
The Administrator reviews the Disclosure Log quarterly and retrains staff on any problems found.
